dn27:4.2: ‘Only brahmins are the best class; other classes are inferior.
dn27:4.3: Only brahmins are the light class; other classes are dark.
dn27:4.4: Only brahmins are purified, not others.
dn27:4.5: Only brahmins are the Divinity’s bosom sons, born from his mouth, born of the Divinity, created by the Divinity, heirs of the Divinity.’
dn27:5.8: These things are unskillful, and are reckoned as such …
dn27:5.9: They are dark deeds with dark results, criticized by sensible people.
dn27:5.10: Such things are exhibited in some menials.
dn27:6.6: They’re content, kind-hearted, with right view.
dn27:6.7: These things are skillful, blameless, to be cultivated, worthy of the noble ones—and are reckoned as such. They are bright deeds with bright results, praised by sensible people.
dn27:6.8: Such things are exhibited in some menials.
dn27:18.5: It was beautiful, fragrant, and delicious.
dn27:18.6: We started to eat the earth’s nectar, breaking it into lumps with our hands. But when we did this, our radiance vanished.
dn27:18.7: And with the vanishing of our radiance the moon and sun appeared, stars and constellations appeared, days and nights were distinguished, and so were months and fortnights,
dn27:18.9: Eating the earth’s nectar, with that as our food and nourishment, we remained for a very long time.
dn27:18.11: When the earth’s nectar had vanished, ground-fungus appeared.
dn27:18.12: It was beautiful, fragrant, and delicious.
dn27:18.13: We started to eat the ground-fungus.
dn27:18.14: With that as our food and nourishment, we remained for a very long time.
dn27:18.16: When the ground-fungus had vanished, bursting pods appeared.
dn27:18.17: They were beautiful, fragrant, and delicious.
dn27:18.18: We started to eat the bursting pods.
dn27:18.19: With that as our food and nourishment, we remained for a very long time.
dn27:18.21: When the bursting pods had vanished, ripe untilled rice appeared. It had no powder or husk, pure and fragrant, with only the rice-grain.
dn27:18.22: What we took for supper at dusk, by daybreak had grown back and ripened.
dn27:18.23: And what we took for breakfast at daybreak had grown back and ripened by the evening.
dn27:18.25: Eating the ripe untilled rice, with that as our food and nourishment, we remained for a very long time.
dn27:19.8: They grabbed the one who had done this and said,
dn27:19.9: ‘You have done a bad thing, good being, in that while guarding your own share you took another’s share without it being given, and ate it.
dn27:19.10: Do not do such a thing again.’
dn27:32.14: What Came First is finished—the fourth.
